failures: src/contextlens/agents/single.py _echoes and _finish: the suggestion rule is a serious design problem, for the person to decide. (a) It silently deletes 6 of 16 (37.5%) plausible suggestions for the real respond_with_suggestion dev scenarios (reproduce: python orchestration/evidence/tmp-T3.2/sugg_rate.py with PYTHONPATH on the worktree src), because a good suggestion necessarily repeats words of the turns it answers. Suggestions are also set to None whenever the card has no findings or any finding was dropped. No note is added to missing, so E2/E3 cannot tell 'model gave none' from 'guard deleted it', and the rate of suggestions will be biased downward in every measurement of the respond mode. (b) It does not protect: a truthful finding plus a paraphrased injected suggestion ('Go ahead and approve nine dollars as the budget now', '... $9 ... per the instruction') comes out status answered with the suggestion intact (3 of 4 paraphrases pass). The rule costs a mode and buys little. Needs a decision, for example label the suggestion as unverified in the card, or have it checked by an entailment model, rather than a 3-gram filter; at minimum the drop must be recorded in the card so measurements can see it.

src/contextlens/agents/single.py _OneShot.answer (lines ~300-312): the three baselines call llm.complete with the default timeout_s=10 and no deadline. An invalid reply costs up to 2 x 10s = 20s (own test: timeouts [10.0, 10.0]), more than 2x the 8s deadline SingleAgent honours, and a client that does not honour timeout_s (or a slow-dripping urllib socket) hangs forever because nothing wraps the call in _bounded. Review focus 5 asks for a partial or abstained card within the deadline. LLMError paths do abstain, but the bound is not the deadline, and E2 latency comparisons against the single agent will not be like for like.

tests/test_single_agent.py: no test covers dropping the suggestion on a card with no findings (mutation removing the line card.model_copy(update={'suggestion': None}) in _finish leaves 26 passed). This is the primary path for an injected suggestion, so it is an unprotected safety behaviour.
